summary: Across the week, global trade dynamics were defined by a dual-track restructuring of Asian supply chains as escalating US tech sanctions and persistent Middle East maritime risks forced a pivot away from traditional long-haul ocean routes. In response, India is aggressively expanding domestic infrastructure and securing allied tech partnerships to reduce reliance on Chinese hardware, while China is fortifying alternative overland corridors and regional free trade pacts across ASEAN and Africa. Continued fuel price volatility and sea-lane disruptions will further accelerate nearshoring efforts and multimodal transport investments across both economies. Ultimately, this points toward a more fragmented regional supply chain landscape where India captures shifted high-tech manufacturing and China solidifies dominance over non-Western trade corridors.
